implementationPlan.description: READ-ONLY (DoD 1). This is the epic's FINAL ACCEPTANCE row; it owns no production file (the affectedFiles are read-only anchors) and it is planned now only so the architect queue stops re-offering it — a worker who claims it before the board is clear blocks at this step, by design. (a) BOARD CENSUS: `moe.list_tasks { epicId: "epic-072d85bea56c4badb07b9356ae195a98" }` — excluding this row, EVERY row must be DONE or ARCHIVED (at planning, 17:12Z: 55 DONE, 4 ARCHIVED, 18 WORKING, 3 BLOCKED, 2 other PLANNING — so this step blocks today). List every non-DONE row by id + status in the block reason; `moe.report_blocked` naming them. Do not treat a parent's children being DONE as the parent being DONE (handoff pitfall). (b) `task-064b97584aff4e07967738f79134a723` (source policy) is DONE at planning — re-confirm. (c) TREE CENSUS at the delivered HEAD: record `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain | wc -l` (this repo tracks its own runtime state under .moe/, so a nonzero count is expected — list every NON-.moe dirty path verbatim; each is foreign WIP to disclose, never adopt), and `git ls-files -v | grep '^S'` (skip-worktree bits — a path so marked reports clean while its bytes differ; list them). Record all of it in a row comment via `moe.add_comment` (the completion summary is write-only). Never edit a production file in this row; DoD 2's 'add or consolidate missing coverage' is discharged by FILING rows (step 8), not by authoring here.

DoD 2. Enumerate mechanically — every DONE row in this epic carries `verification: { command, exitCode, outputTail, reportedAt }` (measured: 55/55 at planning). Run from the repo root: `node -e "const fs=require('fs');for(const f of fs.readdirSync('.moe/tasks')){const t=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('.moe/tasks/'+f,'utf8'));if(t.epicId!=='epic-072d85bea56c4badb07b9356ae195a98'||t.status!=='DONE')continue;console.log(t.order,'|',t.id,'|',t.title.slice(0,60),'|',t.verification.command)}"` — post the roster (id, finding prefix P1.x/P2.x from the title, command) as a comment with the EXACT row count; the count must equal the DONE census from step 1 (a roster shorter than the census means a row without a gate — list it as a residual). Then run EVERY distinct command standalone, foreground, unpiped, exactly as recorded (some use `--root apps/daemon --config package.json`, some `--filter`, one `cargo test`; a `--filter` leg proves execution only by its `Test Files` count line). Record per command: exit code and the count lines. A RED is attributed by file: re-run that file standalone (the root pool is known to flake under load — comment-1d3f1ae3: timeouts + a V8 worker crash that cleared standalone); a red that survives standalone is a RESIDUAL FINDING named by row id and finding number — P1 (findings 1-11) residuals force the request-changes verdict (task rail 3). Group findings: P1.1-P1.11 are merge blockers; P2.12-P2.19 are required follow-ups.

DoD 4. Foreground, unpiped, unchained; quote exit code + `Test Files`/`Tests` (or cargo/node --test) count lines per leg: (1) `pnpm typecheck` (recursive; quote each package's `$ tsc` echo). (2) `pnpm verify:foundation` (typecheck + test:meta). (3) `pnpm verify:store`. (4) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. (5) `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. (6) `pnpm test:security` (tsc gate + lane; the lane compiles on tracked objects since task-fe55a3c1 landed 3dc442e6, and the seven-constant roster gap is task-d1145412's). (7) `pnpm test:fault`. (8) `pnpm test:migration`. (9) `pnpm test:property`. (10) `pnpm test:e2e` and (11) `pnpm test:e2e:browser` (static, daemon-free journey — a red is a regression, not a flake). (12) `pnpm test:integration` (packaging + import typechecks, tests/integration, and the three `node --test` release legs: release-supply-chain, windows-pack-observation, verify-windows-release). (13) `pnpm verify:release` (typecheck:release + test:integration + `release:evidence`). (14) `pnpm test` at the root — record it, but attribute any red by re-running the failing FILES standalone; report both the root result and the standalone results verbatim. CROSS-HOST LANES (.github/workflows/cross-host.yml) cannot be run locally and pushing is forbidden (epic rail 1): cite the newest CI run for the delivered HEAD if one exists (`gh run list --commit <sha>` read-only), else state plainly in the verdict that cross-host evidence is pending CI — never fabricate it.

DoD 3. (a) ARTIFACT: `pnpm pack:windows` (tools/packaging/pack-windows-main.ts) into its default output; then `node scripts/release/verify-windows-release.mjs` with the arguments its own header documents (read the file first; quote the invocation) and `pnpm release:observe-windows-pack`; record exit codes and the observation output. (b) CREDENTIAL SCAN: the production scanner is tools/packaging/pack-source-sensitive.ts (exercised by tools/packaging/pack-source.test.ts — `pnpm exec vitest run tools/packaging/pack-source.test.ts`, nonzero counts); ALSO grep the produced artifact tree and every process/log capture the lanes wrote (`grep -rIl -e "moe-session" -e "Bearer " -e "csrfToken" -e "credentialId" -e "PRIVATE KEY" <artifact-dir> <log-dir>`) — must be EMPTY; any hit is a P1 residual (finding class: credential exposure). (c) TAMPER: the durable-state tamper matrix is the security lane's durable-store-boundaries + integrity-boundaries slices (step 3 leg 6) plus `pnpm test:migration` — confirm by NAME that arms covering decision, recovery, budget, graph and worktree state ran (grep the lane output for `durable-store` and `integrity` slice titles and the migration suite's count line); if any of the five subjects has no arm, list it as a coverage gap for step 8. (d) REAL MCP/UI BOUNDARIES: tests/integration/portability (inside step 3 leg 12) exercises the real MCP host; the browser journey (leg 11) exercises the UI; quote their count lines here again by name. Nothing in this step edits a file; clean the artifact/log directories you created with Bash `rm -rf` and record the paths.

DoD 5. (a) LINE CAP over PRODUCTION sources only: `git ls-files -- 'apps/*/src/**' 'packages/*/src/**' 'adapters/*/src/**' | grep -E '\.(ts|tsx|mjs)$' | grep -vE '\.(test|spec)\.|-fixtures?\.|test-fixtures|/testkit/' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1 > 400 && $2 != "total"'` — must print NOTHING; every hit is a residual naming the file and its owner row (fixture modules are exempt by rule). (b) PROBE ARTIFACTS: `git ls-files | grep -Ei 'probe|scratch|\.tmp$|smoke-[0-9a-f]{8}'` and `find apps packages -maxdepth 3 -name '.project-configuration-smoke-*' -type d` — the boundary-roster header records 21 committed `.project-configuration-smoke-<id>` probe directories under apps/daemon; list every hit verbatim as a residual (deleting them is a separate row — this row edits nothing). (c) DIRTY TREE: the step-1 census of non-.moe dirty paths, each attributed to a live row or marked orphan. (d) `git ls-files -v | grep '^S'` skip-worktree list.

The worktree proves nothing about a clean checkout: `git archive HEAD` into a directory under %TEMP% (never MSYS /tmp; delete afterwards with Bash `rm -rf`), then either `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` there or junction the live node_modules (root and each package), and run: `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` (exit 0), `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts` (count lines), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` inside the materialisation (or their `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --project <pkg>/tsconfig.json` equivalents if `pnpm exec` refuses inside the copy). Any red here that is green in the worktree is a CLEAN-CHECKOUT HOLE — a P1-class residual (untracked bytes the tree depends on); name the missing path from the error text.

For each P1 finding (1-11), take the DONE row's recorded drill (its completion comments name the mutant and the arm that reddened) and re-run ONE narrowest mutant against the delivered tree: mutate the production guard, run only the named arm with `-t`, confirm it reds on the EXACT code/layer the arm's title claims, restore. Tracked paths: `git status --porcelain <path>` before, `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` after. Never stage or commit a mutated path. A GREEN drill is a FINDING (the guard is redundant with a downstream fence, or the arm detached) — record it as a residual for the verdict and file a row in step 8; never bank it. Record the eleven outcomes in a comment (row id, file, mutant, arm, red line or GREEN-FINDING).

Post the FINAL REPORT as row comments (≤4500 chars each, split rather than truncate): (1) HEAD sha, board census, tree census; (2) the reproduction roster with per-row exit/count results; (3) the fourteen lane legs; (4) artifact/credential/tamper/boundary results; (5) hygiene residuals; (6) clean-checkout proof; (7) the eleven drills; (8) VERDICT: `MERGE` only if every P1 finding (1-11) reproduces as fixed, no P1-class residual exists, and the clean-checkout proof is green — otherwise `REQUEST-CHANGES` with the residual list, each residual paired with a filed follow-up row (`moe.create_task`, status PLANNING, one owned path set, verify-or-block DoD 1) or an existing row id. Cross-host lanes are stated as pending CI when not runnable. This row commits NOTHING (it edits nothing; a finished row may have no commit). Do not merge, push or post a PR review (task rail 2).

When you re-run the R3-12 reproduction, cite THIS row's evidence together with task-861530ae's (half A). Delivered by half B at commit 87f005d0 (branch moe/work-2026-08-08), four owned paths:
- tools/packaging/authenticate-node.ps1 (NEW, 130 lines) - resolves node from RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE rather than PATH, compares Get-FileHash SHA256 and `node --version` to the single tracked pin, then launches with shell-free argv. Refuses WINDOWS_RELEASE_INPUT_INVALID / WINDOWS_RELEASE_NODE_DIGEST_MISMATCH / WINDOWS_RELEASE_VERSION_MISMATCH, all at layer WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY.
- .github/workflows/reusable-windows-candidate-build.yml - the ZIP step and the evidence step now call that script; 392 lines against the contract-asserted 400 cap; zero residual `pnpm pack:windows` / `pnpm release:evidence`.
- tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs (NEW) - the end-to-end forged-pnpm harness.
- tests/integration/release/release-workflow-contract.test.ts - 4 new arms (30 total).

Gates you can re-run verbatim, all EXIT 0 at the delivered tree: `pnpm typecheck:release`; `pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/release/release-workflow-contract.test.ts` (`Tests 30 passed (30)`); `node --test tests/integration/release/verify-windows-release.test.mjs` (`tests 37 / pass 37`); `node --test tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` (`tests 1 / pass 1`).

ONE FINDING YOU MUST CARRY, because it changes where the reproduction has to cut. The plan's drill named scripts/release/pnpm-runner.mjs as the guard the pack path crosses. It does NOT. Reverting the digest check there leaves the harness GREEN. The pack path's refusal - `PACK_STEP_FAILED: pnpm provenance invalid` - is emitted by tools/packaging/pack-command.ts:193/198/210 (`resolvePnpmPackTool`); pnpm-runner.mjs gates the release-evidence/supply-chain path instead. Drilled at the correct seam in a %TEMP% tree copy, the harness reds and the forged pnpm visibly executes `$ pnpm "install" "--frozen-lockfile" "--ignore-scripts"`. If your reproduction cuts at pnpm-runner.mjs for the PACK path it will report a false green.

Two disclosed limits: the harness asserts the staged node's digest equals the pin, so on a Windows host whose node is not the pinned build it reds environmentally rather than skipping; and a pre-existing tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs sits one directory above the new one, so select by full path, never by basename.
